title: ibn-abd-al-barr rejects innate-knowledge
text: That a child is born knowing God 'is what observation and reason belie'; the most correct reading is soundness and uprightness. Yet he grants, as the consensus of Ahl al-Sunna, an inborn pull toward a Creator once reason matures.

title: ibn-taymiyya qualifies innate-knowledge
text: The fitra contains acknowledging and loving the Creator, as a newborn desires the milk that suits it; but it is not knowledge of the religion at birth; it develops, and messengers complete it.

title: ibn-al-qayyim affirms la-tabdil
text: What people are born upon is God's creation, which no one but He could replace, and He does not; unlike exchanging unbelief for faith, which happens often.

title: mujahid rejects la-tabdil
text: 'No changing God's creation' means God's religion: a command not to change it, not a statement that it cannot be replaced.

title: tabari rejects la-tabdil
text: Reads lā tabdīl as no taghyīr of God's religion, a prohibition; he does not distinguish tabdīl from taghyīr.
